head: 105f1a4c870f7995acbe4b668bb2102d694b9d1d
summary:
All 14 acceptance criteria hold on this tree (105f1a4), and O-013 and O-014 are discharged by my own runs. The verdict is partial, not passes, because O-015 is still open. It is the code-review fix owed to build-slice, and I reproduced the defect on this tree.

What passed:
- Core tests: 120/120.
- Fitness: 20 rules hold, including the three SL-033 rules.
- rules-parity: AGREE.
- WindowCases -Case All: all 15 cases passed in 161 s. C-006 stopped at 550 of 30,150 folders. C-012 and O-016 each exited 70 and removed the planted stale report.
- The design's 30-run repeat against the committed hook, on one warm tree:
  - stop: 30/30 acted, exit 0, schema-1 report, Cancelled with a "Stopped:" title, scan stopped at 550–750 of 30,150 folders.
  - close: 30/30 acted, exit 70, no report, stale report gone.
  - throw: 30/30 acted, exit 70, no report, stale report gone.
  - Every acted line showed enabled=True visible=True, and no hook variable was left set afterwards.
- WindowMutants -Mutant All passed in 182 s. StopDisabled and StopCollapsed each failed C-006 only on "the hook acted". NoCrashHandler failed C-012 on 0xE0434352. NoExitRule failed O-016 on exit 0. HookCompileError and HookLocked each stopped the run in Update-Hook, and the old dll was left unchanged.

My own probes:
- Criterion 13: an unknown mode ("bogus", and "STOP" in capitals) logs "refused ... unknown mode" and does nothing. The app still finishes (Completed), and CheckActed fails.
- Criterion 14: a relative dll path, and a path containing ';', both make the host fail at startup with 0xE0434352 and write no log line, so CheckActed fails. The committed $HookDll is absolute, and the repo path has no ';'.
- Real lock: a real FsAnalyser.App.exe with the scratch hook dll loaded made Update-Hook fail with MSB3027 "locked by FsAnalyser.App (31620)". The run exited 1 and the dll was unchanged.

O-015 reproduced: I mutated OnCancel in a scratch copy to throw. Under stop mode the hook logged 'acted' and then 'refused ... InvalidOperationException'. The app scanned 30,150 of 30,150 folders, wrote a Finished report and exited 0, and C-006 still printed "ok exit code" and "ok a report was written". The exception never reached the app's DispatcherUnhandledException handler. StartupHook.cs:109-120 still calls Act inside Dispatcher.Invoke without re-raising, and CheckActed (WindowCases.ps1) still ignores a 'refused' line that comes after 'acted'. No committed case passes wrongly because of it, but the driver hides a fault in the app's own handler, and the tree slice will reuse this path.

No loop: one build attempt and one review.

checks.evidence: 10.0.401 (the .dotnet/ the build stage installed under Q-003); artifacts/publish/FsAnalyser.App.exe 139,777,176 bytes is newer than every src file, so Update-App did not republish.
Passed! Failed 0, Passed 120, Skipped 0, Total 120, 9 s.
20 rule(s) checked against 46 file(s); every declared rule holds, including the three SL-033 rules (no test seam in src, no shared code between hook and app, the hook never produces the exit code).
rules-parity: AGREE 7 facts <- 10 twinned entries, 21 patterns; exit 0.

checks.what: Full window suite, including the three hooked cases
checks.evidence: exit 0 in 161 s. PASSED: C-001..C-014 and O-016 (15 cases). C-006: pwsh control exited 0xE0434352; the inert host exited 0 with an empty log; cleanup removed all 3 variables; the no-scan step logged 'waiting found=True enabled=True visible=False' and then refused after 20 s; the main run acted at ms=829 and stopped after 550 of 30150 folders with a 'Stopped:' title. C-012 acted at ms=573 and exited 70 (0x46) with the stale report gone and no .tmp. O-016 acted at ms=642 and exited 70 with the stale report gone and no .tmp.

checks.what: Stop mode, 30 runs against the committed hook on one warm 30,150-folder tree (functions taken from WindowCases.ps1 by AST, so Invoke-HookedRun is the committed code)
checks.evidence: runs=30, acted once in 30, refused 0, exit 0 x30, reports 30, core.status Cancelled x30, OutcomeTitle 'Stopped: <root>' x30, scan stopped at 550-750 of 30150 folders, wall time 546-1401 ms, no variable left set.

checks.what: Close mode, 30 runs, stale report planted each time
checks.evidence: runs=30, acted once in 30, refused 0, exit 70 x30, reports 0, stale report gone 30/30, .tmp absent 30/30, 455-1120 ms.

checks.what: Throw mode, 30 runs, stale report planted each time
checks.evidence: runs=30, acted once in 30, refused 0, exit 70 x30, reports 0, stale report gone 30/30, .tmp absent 30/30. Across all 90 runs every acted line read enabled=True visible=True, acted at ms=336-917, and no run logged 'waiting'.

checks.what: Mutation proofs: each hooked case fails against its mutant, once, for the planted reason
checks.evidence: exit 0 in 182 s. StopDisabled: the hook saw 'enabled=False visible=True' and never acted; C-006's single FAIL was 'the hook acted'. StopCollapsed: never visible; the same single FAIL. NoCrashHandler: the hook acted and C-012 failed once with 'actual -532462766 (0xE0434352)'. NoExitRule: the hook acted and O-016 failed once with 'actual 0 (0x00000000)'. HookCompileError: CS1029 printed, Update-Hook stopped the run, C-006 never started, old dll unchanged. HookLocked: MSB3021/3027 printed and the result was the same. No scratch copies were left in %TEMP%\fsa-window-mutants.

bogus: log 'loaded mode=bogus | refused mode=bogus reason=unknown mode', exit 0, report Completed, CheckActed FAIL. STOP: the same (the match is case-sensitive), Completed, CheckActed FAIL. The hook did nothing and the app ran normally.
exit -532462766 (0xE0434352), no report, empty log, CheckActed FAIL. The run cannot pass silently.

checks.command: probe-13-14.ps1 with the dll copied into a folder named 'with;semi'
checks.evidence: exit 0xE0434352, no report, empty log, CheckActed FAIL. The repo path contains no ';' (False), and $HookDll is fully qualified (True).

checks.what: Update-Hook against a real leftover FsAnalyser.App.exe holding the dll (not the FileStream stand-in)
checks.evidence: The app (pid 31620) was alive with FsaWindowHook.dll in its module list. The scratch WindowCases -Case C-006 exited 1 with 'error MSB3027 ... The file is locked by: "FsAnalyser.App (31620)"'; the dll hash was unchanged. I did not see the 'FAILED: the hook did not build' line in my filtered output (my Select -First cut it off). Exit 1, and the absence of a C-006 header, agree with the committed HookLocked assertions.

My own mutation was wrong: '_cancel?.Cancel();' matches twice in MainWindow.xaml.cs (OnClosing:52 and OnCancel:225), and Set-Mutation refused it. I narrowed it to OnCancel's two lines and re-ran. This says nothing about the slice.

checks.what: O-015 probe: an exception thrown by OnCancel under hook stop mode (scratch copy, republished)
checks.evidence: hook log: 'acted mode=stop enabled=True visible=True ms=528' then 'refused mode=stop reason=InvalidOperationException: validate mutant: OnCancel threw'. The case printed 'ok exit code' (0) and 'ok a report was written', then FAIL core.status and FAIL OutcomeTitle ('Finished: ...'), stopped after 30150 of 30150 folders. The exception never reached App.DispatcherUnhandledException, so the O-015 defect is present on this tree.

checks.what: Static read of the O-015 fix site
checks.evidence: Act(mode, app, button) is still called inside app.Dispatcher.Invoke(..., DispatcherPriority.Normal) with no inner try/catch and no ExceptionDispatchInfo re-raise through BeginInvoke. CheckActed still counts only 'acted mode=' lines and ignores a later 'refused'. Neither part of O-015's fix is in the tree (build-slice's only attempt is at 105f1a4, which is before the review).

checks.command: Test-Path %TEMP%\fsa-window-{mutants,cases,hook}; Get-Process FsAnalyser.App; env; git status --short
checks.evidence: All three temp folders are empty; 0 FsAnalyser.App processes; 0 hook variables set; git status shows only the pre-existing .taad/slices/SL-033 changes.

checks.what: A real mouse or UIA press on CancelButton, to show a throwing handler exits 70 through real input
checks.evidence: The stack rules out UIA, FlaUI and WinAppDriver, and I may not drive another program's windows. That a real click reaches DispatcherUnhandledException is reasoning about WPF. The nearest measured path is throw mode's BeginInvoke exception, which exits 70 (30/30).

criteria.criterion: 1. stop the scan (C-006) when Stop is pressable and the scan is running on the 30,150-folder New-LargeTree
criteria.how: C-006 in -Case All passed, and my 30-run repeat gave 30/30 acted, exit 0, schema-1, Cancelled, 'Stopped:' title, scan stopped at 550-750 of 30,150 folders.

criteria.criterion: 2. stop the scan (C-006) when the scan finishes before the hook acts
criteria.how: The warm-cache repeat never let the scan win (worst case 750 of 30,150 folders). In the StopCollapsed mutant run, where the scan did finish without the hook acting, C-006's only FAIL was 'the hook acted', not an ending mismatch: CheckActed runs first and returns early.

criteria.criterion: 3. stop the scan (C-006) when CancelButton is IsEnabled=false during the scan (scratch mutant)
criteria.how: WindowMutants -Mutant All, StopDisabled: the hook logged 'waiting found=True enabled=False visible=True' and never acted. C-006 exited 1, failing once on 'the hook acted'.

criteria.criterion: 4. stop the scan (C-006) when CancelButton is Visibility=Collapsed during the scan (scratch mutant)
criteria.how: StopCollapsed: never visible, never acted. C-006 exited 1, failing once on 'the hook acted'.

criteria.criterion: 5. stop the scan (C-006) when CancelButton is pressable before StartScan begins (XAML default is enabled)
criteria.how: C-006's no-scan step (in -Case All): the window opened with no root, the hook logged 'waiting found=True enabled=True visible=False', did not act, and refused after 20 s. In the 90 repeat runs the hook's first look was already mid-scan (no 'waiting' lines).

criteria.criterion: 6. exit-70 path (C-012) on an unhandled dispatcher exception mid-scan, handler present, stale report planted
criteria.how: C-012 in -Case All passed (acted ms=573, exit 70 (0x46), stale report gone, no .tmp). Throw repeat: exit 70 in 30/30, stale report gone 30/30.

criteria.criterion: 7. exit-70 path (C-012) with the DispatcherUnhandledException handler removed (scratch mutant)
criteria.how: NoCrashHandler: the hook acted and C-012 failed exactly once with 'actual -532462766 (0xE0434352)'.

criteria.criterion: 8. closed before the first ending (O-016): window closed while Stop is pressable, report mode, stale report planted
criteria.how: O-016 in -Case All passed (acted ms=642, exit 70, stale report gone, no .tmp). Close repeat: exit 70 in 30/30, 0 reports, stale report gone 30/30.

criteria.criterion: 9. closed before the first ending (O-016) with the Exit handler's exit-0-without-a-file to 70 rule removed (scratch mutant)
criteria.how: NoExitRule: the hook acted and O-016 failed exactly once with 'actual 0 (0x00000000)'.

criteria.criterion: 10. hooked run cleanup when a case throws or fails after the three variables are set
criteria.how: C-006's cleanup step passed (the throw reached the case; all 3 variables removed). After 90 hooked repeat runs and all probes, 0 hook variables were left set.

criteria.criterion: 11. load the hook: a non-App .NET host inherits the variables (pwsh 7 with FSA_HOOK_MODE=close)
criteria.how: In -Case All the control (missing dll) made pwsh exit 0xE0434352, which shows pwsh loads startup hooks. Under the real hook pwsh exited 0 and the log stayed empty.

criteria.criterion: 12. build the hook: compile error, or dll locked by a leftover FsAnalyser.App.exe
criteria.how: The HookCompileError and HookLocked mutants passed. I also used a real FsAnalyser.App.exe (pid 31620) with the dll loaded: Update-Hook's build failed with MSB3027 naming it, the scratch run exited 1, and the dll was unchanged.

criteria.criterion: 13. select a mode: FSA_HOOK_MODE is an unknown string
criteria.how: The design outcome was: log 'refused' and do nothing. Measured with 'bogus' and 'STOP': 'refused mode=... reason=unknown mode', the app ran to Completed with exit 0, and CheckActed would fail the case.

criteria.criterion: 14. locate the hook dll: the path is relative, or contains ';'
criteria.how: The design outcome was: the committed path is absolute and has no ';', and a wrong path shows as a failed 'acted' check. Measured: $HookDll is fully qualified and the repo path has no ';'. A relative path and a ';' path each made the host fail at startup (0xE0434352) with an empty log, and CheckActed failed.

obligations.evidence: The shim cannot produce the outcome, measured against the committed hook: NoCrashHandler made throw mode exit 0xE0434352 (C-012 failed once), and NoExitRule made close mode exit 0 (O-016 failed once), so neither 70 comes from the hook. Fitness rule 'the hook never produces the outcome under test' holds (no Environment.Exit/FailFast, .Shutdown( or ExitCode= in the hook source). Unmutated: throw 30/30 and close 30/30 exited 70.

The shim meets the user's gate: the StopDisabled and StopCollapsed mutants each made C-006 fail on 'the hook acted' (no act through a disabled or hidden button). The no-scan step showed an enabled but hidden CancelButton was not pressed. The gate coincided with a running scan in every one of 30 stop runs: Cancelled at 550-750 of 30,150 folders. All 90 acted lines read enabled=True visible=True.

Owed to build-slice, not fixed. StartupHook.cs:109-120 still runs Act inside Dispatcher.Invoke with no inner catch and no BeginInvoke re-raise, and CheckActed still ignores a 'refused' line after 'acted'. Reproduced in a scratch copy with OnCancel throwing: log 'acted mode=stop ...' then 'refused mode=stop reason=InvalidOperationException: validate mutant: OnCancel threw'; scan ran 30150/30150, Finished report, exit 0; C-006 printed 'ok exit code' and 'ok a report was written' before failing on core.status. The app's DispatcherUnhandledException never saw the exception. build-slice's only attempt (105f1a4) is before the review that raised this.

not_reached: A real input-driven press (mouse or UIA) on a CancelButton whose handler throws. O-015's premise, that a real click would reach DispatcherUnhandledException and exit 70, is reasoning about WPF, not something I measured.

A machine where Windows Error Reporting shows a crash dialog: with SetErrorMode dropped, a regressed crash handler there would show C-012 as TIMEOUT rather than 0xE0434352. Here the process ended at once.
Windows 10. Everything ran on Windows 11 26200 only.
Other .NET hosts inheriting the hook variables (dotnet.exe, MSBuild nodes). Only pwsh 7.6.6 on .NET 10.0.12 was checked. Update-Hook builds before any variable is set.
Slower or faster disks and CPUs. The hook acted at 336-917 ms with the scan at 550-750 of 30,150 folders here. On a much faster machine the margin before the scan finishes is unmeasured.
Any real user data or drive. Every run used generated trees under %TEMP%, which is why contact is graded code, not real.
